summary: The simulation is structurally sound but contains critical logic flaws in daily update ordering and mask-use gating that distort compliance dynamics. Additional issues include inefficient lookups, incomplete enforcement effects, ignored parameters, missing metrics, and some dead/fragile code. Reordering the daily loop, gating mask wearing on inventory/household allocation, implementing budget-deducting fines, adding ID maps for O(1) lookups, honoring locations_count_by_type, and computing missing metrics will substantially improve correctness, performance, and alignment with the model plan.

critical_issues.issue: Daily update order uses mobility/enforcement before behavior decisions, so location compliance and enforcement are computed from stale mask states.
critical_issues.impact: Compliance rates, enforcement prompts, and peer/observation influence are misaligned with actual same-day decisions, biasing adoption dynamics and delaying policy/media effects.
critical_issues.solution: Reorder run loop to: policy_module.update() -> info_module.update() -> behavior_module.update() -> mobility_module.update() -> retail_module.update() -> aggregator.update(). Ensure last_observed_compliance is used as a lagged variable (yesterday’s observation) and prompted_today is set by mobility for next day.

critical_issues.issue: Agents can adopt (mask_use_state=1) without owning a mask; purchases happen later.
critical_issues.impact: Overstates same-day compliance and underestimates the role of supply/budget constraints.
critical_issues.solution: Gate wearing on available mask_ownership or immediate household allocation. If not available, generate a purchase intent and keep mask_use_state=0 for the current day.

critical_issues.issue: Fines are recorded but not deducted from household budgets.
critical_issues.impact: Enforcement has no economic consequence; therefore, it cannot influence future purchasing/behavior realistically.
critical_issues.solution: On fine, find the person’s household and deduct fine_amount, clamped at zero; record deduction in event.

critical_issues.issue: O(N) linear lookups for agent/household in hot loops.
critical_issues.impact: Poor scalability and avoidable CPU cost; risk of StopIteration exceptions.
critical_issues.solution: Maintain persistent dicts: id_to_agent and person_id_to_household. Replace next(...) usages with dict lookups.

model_improvements.current_approach: Behavior uses same-day last_observed_compliance set by mobility that was computed from yesterday’s mask states.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Use last_observed_compliance as a lagged signal (yesterday’s observation). Apply enforcement prompts after behavior; their effect (prompted_today) should apply next day unless explicit immediate compliance logic is added.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Causally consistent day structure; avoids feedback artifacts.

model_improvements.current_approach: Agents can wear without inventory; purchases are processed afterward.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Adoption requires mask availability (own or household allocation). If none, log purchase intent and keep not wearing today.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: More realistic coupling between supply, budget, and adoption trajectory.

model_improvements.current_approach: Household budget set by household SES but person SES assigned independently.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Assign household SES and propagate to members by default; allow mild noise if needed.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Consistent SES-linked behaviors (budget, adoption disparity) and clearer attribution in disparity metrics.

model_improvements.current_approach: locations_count_by_type is ignored; split keys are used.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Honor locations_count_by_type with split keys as fallback.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Closer adherence to the model plan and more flexible scenario control.

model_improvements.suggested_approach: Add peak adoption and post-mandate sustained adoption among required metrics.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Better alignment with planned evaluation and policy-relevant outputs.

code_improvements.modification: Reorder daily updates so behavior decisions occur before mobility/enforcement, and use previous day’s avg_price and last_observed_compliance.
code_improvements.reason: Fixes critical causality bug and ensures compliance reflects current-day decisions.

code_improvements.modification: Gate mask wearing on actual inventory or immediate household allocation; generate purchase intent if none available; do not allow wearing without mask.
code_improvements.reason: Prevents overestimation of adoption on supply-constrained days.

code_improvements.modification: Introduce id_to_agent and person_id_to_household maps; use them in compliance/enforcement; deduct fines from household budgets; update last_observed_compliance after behavior for use next day.
code_improvements.reason: Improves performance and correctness; implements economic consequences of enforcement.

code_improvements.modification: Compute peak_adoption and sustained_adoption_post_mandate; include in evaluation outputs.
code_improvements.reason: Completes planned metrics for better evaluation.

code_improvements.modification: Honor locations_count_by_type param; remove initial dead household creation block; align person SES with household SES.
code_improvements.reason: Cleaner initialization; plan compliance; coherent SES relationships.

code_improvements.modification: Avoid next(...) without default; remove unused vars and redundant pass statements; precompute and reuse maps in modules.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Likely underestimated due to same-day wearing without inventory and stale compliance feedback.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Gate wearing on inventory and reorder day updates; calibrate peer/policy/media weights to published adoption curves for similar mandates.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: SES not coherently tied to household budgets/person SES; subsidies not targeted in a nuanced way.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Assign SES at household level, propagate to members, and test targeted subsidies/distribution to low SES; validate disparity trends against survey data.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Computed from previous-day behavior under current ordering; overstates effects or lags improperly.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Compute after same-day behavior decisions; add location-type-specific enforcement sensitivities to match observed compliance variation by venue.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Habit/abandonment rates not calibrated; likely misrepresent sustained adoption post-mandate.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Calibrate habit_formation_rate and abandonment_rate to panel/survey evidence; consider decay with heterogeneity by attitude/trust.

prioritized_actions: Reorder Simulation.run daily loop so behavior precedes mobility/enforcement.
Enforce inventory gating for mask wearing and household allocation-attempt before setting mask_use_state=1.
Implement fine deduction from household budgets in enforcement.
Introduce id_to_agent and person_id_to_household maps; replace linear searches.
Compute missing metrics (peak_adoption, sustained_adoption_post_mandate) and honor locations_count_by_type.
Clean initialization: remove dead household creation, align person SES with household SES.
Harden error handling (avoid next without default) and remove unused code.
additional_comments: The direct call to main() at the end is acceptable per sandbox requirements. Consider adding unit tests for day ordering and mask gating to prevent regressions. Also consider adding a two-stage behavior update (pre-visit intent; post-enforcement compliance) if modeling on-the-spot compliance is desired.

    def summarize_metrics(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        df = self.to_dataframe()
        peak_adoption = float(df["adoption_rate"].max()) if not df.empty else 0.0
        mandate_end = int(self.params.get("mandate_end_day", 90))
        post = df[df["day"] > mandate_end]
        sustained_adoption = float(post["adoption_rate"].mean()) if not post.empty else None
        return {"peak_adoption": peak_adoption, "sustained_adoption_post_mandate": sustained_adoption}

change_analysis.summary: The current code appears to be a baseline implementation without prior diffs, but the structure suggests some incremental assembly. The main negative impacts are logical ordering and gating oversights. Positive aspects include modularization and an embedded plan that mostly drives parameters.
positive_impacts: Clear modular separation (policy, info, mobility, retail, behavior, aggregator).
Use of RNG with seed consistency across modules.
Inclusion of social network and multiple interaction channels.
negative_impacts: Daily update order misaligns decisions and outcomes.
Resource constraints are not respected in same-day adoption.
Performance issues from repeated linear searches.
Some parameters from the model plan are ignored.
suggestions: Reorder daily loop and treat observation/enforcement as lagged signals for next-day behavior.
Gate mask wearing on inventory or household allocation; otherwise generate purchase intent.
Introduce and reuse id maps for O(1) lookups in high-frequency loops.
Honor locations_count_by_type and compute missing metrics to match plan.
